title: Swahili Egg Curry
community: Swahili coast — the coastal egg preparation
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Swahili Egg Curry — hard-boiled eggs halved and simmered in a rich Zanzibar spice and coconut milk sauce. The coastal egg preparation that makes the most of eggs — simple protein elevated by the full coastal flavour palette.
longDesc: Egg curry on the Swahili coast uses the same coconut-spice sauce base as fish and meat curries — but the egg absorbs the curry beautifully, producing a deeply flavoured result from the simplest and most affordable protein.
steps: Cook onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, and all spices.
Add tomatoes. Cook 6—8 minutes until thick.
Add coconut milk. Bring to gentle simmer.
Add egg halves cut-side down. Spoon sauce over.
chefTips: Score the egg whites lightly before adding — allows sauce to penetrate.
Cut-side down into the sauce first — absorbs better.
cookingScience: Hard-boiled egg white is a dense protein matrix. Scoring the surface creates channels that allow the sauce to penetrate into the egg. The scored surface also provides more area for the Maillard reaction with the sauce, creating flavour bonding.
sustainabilityTips: Eggs are among the most sustainable animal proteins.
culturalNote: Egg curry is the coast's most affordable complete protein dish — when fish is unavailable or too expensive, eggs in the same Zanzibar spice coconut sauce provide every flavour of the coast at a fraction of the cost.
